meta.title: Controllability and observability of a bridge circuit
meta.tools: Controllability/observability matrices and their rank, Gramians via Lyapunov equations, singular values as a quantitative measure, pole-zero cancellation
meta.summary: Build a symmetric RC bridge in which one internal mode cannot be driven from the input when the bridge is balanced; show the rank deficiency, the resulting pole-zero cancellation in the transfer function, and how a small imbalance restores full rank but leaves the mode 'nearly uncontrollable' (tiny Gramian singular value).
meta.problem: Can a circuit have internal dynamics that no input can excite — and does that show up anywhere measurable?
meta.theory:
Controllable iff rank [B, AB, …, A^{n−1}B] = n. In a symmetric circuit driven symmetrically, the antisymmetric mode (difference of the two capacitor voltages) obeys an equation with no input term, so it is
uncontrollable; its pole cancels in the transfer function to a symmetric output. Near balance (imbalance ε) the smallest singular value of the controllability Gramian $W_c$ (AW + WAᵀ + BBᵀ = 0) scales
like ε², a quantitative 'distance' from losing controllability.
meta.method: Two RC branches (R1, C1) and (R2, C2) from the input to ground via a coupling resistor R_c between the capacitor nodes; states v1, v2; output (v1+v2)/2 or v1−v2. ε = (R2−R1)/R1 from 0 to 10 %.
